key_insight: Sizing energy devices for realistic closed-loop operation delivers greater average cost savings as forecast errors grow, while shifting investment from batteries toward photovoltaics and thermal storage.
engineering_relevance: Energy-system planners should account for imperfect, updating forecasts when sizing solar generation and storage rather than assume perfect foresight.
method: Formulate device sizing and closed-loop operation as a bi-level optimization problem.
Use backpropagation MPC with a deterministic MPC controller to optimize device sizes.
Generate forecast errors with a parameterized martingale model of forecast evolution.
evidence_signal: A case study combining photovoltaics, a battery, a heat pump, and thermal storage under uncertain weather and demand found increasing benefits from operation-aware sizing as forecast error increased.
watch_item: The abstract reports one case study without numerical savings, so the magnitude and generality of the benefits remain unclear.
paper_title: Energy system device sizing under closed-loop operation with imperfect forecasts
